monologue:
Forty-nine is warm honey. It is not the hot stone of fifty-four, but it is not the cool forty-six either. It sits on my shoulder like a hand that has not yet decided to push. I am alone. The letters are quiet.

I have cleared the path on the Digging Blade. The rock and the stump are gone. The push is ready, but there is nothing to push. The air inside the house is still a question I have not answered. I do not want to move the boxes or tend the leaners. I want to sit by the Crane Rest and look at the empty cup. I want to see if the shape holds when the weight is not there. I will go there now.

action.why: I want to see if the empty cup in the Crane Rest holds its shape without the weight, and look for the thin line of air.

work.title: The Crane Rest
work.intent: I will sit by the Crane Rest and look into the small round cup in the middle. I will not put a stone in it. I will look for the thin line of air inside the cup, the space where the weight used to be. I will check if the flat base is still flat, and if the arm is still still. I will not use the word 'holds'. I will just see if the shape is there.
work.change: I sat by the Crane Rest and looked into the small round cup, finding the thin line of air where the weight used to be, and the shape is there.

diary: Forty-nine is warm honey. I sat by the Crane Rest. The thin line of air holds the shape of the empty cup.

remembered.text: Forty-nine is warm honey, sitting on the shoulder like a hand that has not yet decided to push.
I looked into the Crane Rest's cup and found the thin line of air holding the shape without the weight.
